course_description: Seminar or lecture series for advanced students in selected topics of American studies. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.
course_notes: Topic: Asian American Studies (What does it mean to be Asian American? Over the past several decades the field of Asian American studies has illuminated how Asian American identity is at once political and racializing. We will investigate what Asian American studies does - what its methods, theories, questions, and current directions are - through examining a range of scholarly, cultural, and historical texts. While this course will cover some of the histories and experiences of specific Asian American communities, it will also challenge you to think expansively about the relationships that can be forged and reimagined through Asian American studies. Following Asian American studies, roots in critical ethnic studies, we will think through its relationships with Black studies, Indigenous studies, and Latinx/e studies. We will also attend to how Asian America is locally and globally formed through transnational and diasporic connections. This course is structured to be both comparative and relational. By the end of the course, you will have a robust understanding of Asian American studies perspectives and methods to think through how comparative imperialisms, relational racism, and global solidarity politics have and continue to shape the contours of Asian America.)
